references.text: Earlier in the same speech, Jesus says that when these things begin to happen, the disciples should stand up and lift their heads, for their redemption is drawing near ([ref:Luk 21:28|Luke 21:28]). Verse 31 expands on this by linking the signs to the fact that the kingdom of God is near.
The parallel passage in Matthew where Jesus says that when you see all these things, you should know that he is near and standing at the door ([ref:Matt 24:33|Matthew 24:33]).
The parallel passage in Mark where Jesus says that when you see these things happening, then you should know that he is near and standing at the door ([ref:Mark 13:29|Mark 13:29]).

The immediate context with the parable of the fig tree: When the trees sprout leaves, you know that summer is near ([ref:Luk 21:29-30|Luke 21:29-30]). Verse 31 provides the key to interpretation – in the same way, the signs testify that the kingdom of God is near.

When Jesus sends out the seventy, they are to proclaim: "The kingdom of God has come near to you" ([ref:Luk 10:9-11|Luke 10:9-11]). The expression "the kingdom of God is near" is used here in the context of preaching, just as in 21:31 it is linked to the signs of the end times.

Jesus says that the kingdom of God does not come in such a way that one can see it with the eyes, for the kingdom of God is among you ([ref:Luk 17:20-21|Luke 17:20-21]). This complements the understanding of the coming of the kingdom of God in 21:31.

James exhorts: "Be patient, for the coming of the Lord is near ... the judge stands at the door" ([ref:Jak 5:8-9|James 5:8-9]). The same expectation that the coming and judgment of the Lord are near, as in Jesus' words about the nearness of the kingdom of God.
In Revelation it is emphasized that the time is near ([ref:Åp 1:3|Revelation 1:3]). This expectation that fulfillment is near corresponds to Jesus' words that the kingdom of God is near.

Daniel's vision of the Son of Man who receives dominion and a kingdom that will never be destroyed ([ref:Dan 7:13-14|Daniel 7:13-14]). This is the background for the coming of the kingdom of God that Jesus speaks about.

John the Baptist proclaimed: "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near" ([ref:Matt 3:2|Matthew 3:2]). The message of the nearness of the kingdom of God is a recurring theme in the Gospels and points forward to the final fulfillment in Luke 21:31.

Jesus began his ministry by proclaiming: "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near" ([ref:Matt 4:17|Matthew 4:17]). The nearness of the kingdom of God is at the heart of Jesus' preaching, and in Luke 21:31 it is linked to the eschatological signs.
